claims.text: Convex hull analysis of spatial response embeddings can quantify uncertainty in large language models by measuring output dispersion and variability.
Uncertainty in large language models depends on prompt complexity.
Uncertainty in large language models depends on the specific language model evaluated.
Uncertainty in large language models depends on the temperature setting.

evidence.description: The proposed method leverages the spatial properties of response embeddings to measure the dispersion and variability of model outputs.
Experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the prompt complexity.
Experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the model.
Experimental results indicate that the uncertainty of the model for LLMs depends on the temperature setting.

methodologies.name: Geometric Uncertainty Quantification via Convex Hull Analysis
methodologies.description: Generates multiple responses across temperature settings and prompt categories, transforms responses into high-dimensional BERT embeddings, projects to 2D via PCA, clusters using DBSCAN, and calculates convex hulls for clusters to measure dispersion.

limitations.text: Traditional methods for uncertainty quantification, such as probabilistic models and ensemble techniques, face challenges when applied to the complex and high-dimensional nature of LLM-generated outputs.
